# Refresh popup drop geometry when its active target is resized

## Context and problem

The operator asked whether a popup's drop zones adjust after the popup is enlarged. Two sequences were tested while validating #18398 on `d9ea7a5b44` plus its bounded staging changes:

- **Resize before a new hover: passes.** The new permanent native journey enlarges the target, verifies its menu/preview rectangles against actual DOM geometry, and transfers another popup into an area beyond the target's former right edge.
- **Resize an already-hovered target: fails.** A native hover first warms the target's geometry at **146 px** wide. Resize that same native window to **520 px**, keep the source corner inside the former target bounds, then inspect the next native frames. The DOM width is 520; `ownedAffordances.geometry.hostRect.width` remains 146. The direct width assertion fails after 4.7 seconds.

The probe used headed Chrome, on-screen CDP window moves/resizing, the real movement poll and the real default Participation path. No geometry or runtime code was injected. This is a warm-cache invalidation defect, distinct from the staging repair and from the intended result-region preview size.

## Architectural reality and fix

`Participation.defaultPreviewFor` reuses `DragAffordances.ensureGeometry`. The controller memoizes a geometry promise and synchronous mirror until invalidated. Its shared candidate selector can rebuild from a new measured rect, but it cannot discover a resize while the existing geometry is reused.

Make the existing default target/controller invalidate and refresh its geometry when its rendering host changes size during an active gesture. Keep the geometry-generation fence so an old asynchronous measurement cannot overwrite the new size. Preserve the current indicator-first policy and borrowed/owned lifecycle contract; no second geometry cache or popup-specific controller.

| Surface | Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Default target geometry | Actual host geometry and existing DragAffordances generation | Refresh menu, preview and selection after live resize | Pending/unmeasurable geometry must not commit using stale bounds | Changed method JSDoc | Warm-cache native resize regression |
| Candidate selection | Shared registered PreviewContract and producer | Resolve against the refreshed target rect | Existing rejection/leave path | Existing controller docs | Actual DOM/menu/preview alignment and transfer/cancel controls |

Decision Record impact: aligned-with ADR 0029; transient display geometry remains outside durable topology. Structural pre-flight: expected existing-owner changes only. Agent OS structure map N/A.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC-1: warm target geometry with a native hover, resize the target substantially, and observe the next settled menu/preview bounds matching the new actual DOM geometry without leaving/re-entering to force a clear.
- [ ] AC-2: stale in-flight geometry cannot overwrite the newer measurement or authorize a stale-bound drop.
- [ ] AC-3: the resize-before-hover positive from #18398 remains green; unchanged-size frames reuse the current geometry rather than measuring every frame.
- [ ] AC-4: land a permanent headed regression for active-hover resize, with a failing pre-fix control and actual target selection/terminal evidence.

## Out of scope

The native staging repair #18398, independent full roots, native claim-arbiter redesign, broad Workspace decomposition, module-wide class conversion, Feed virtual-row census, or new persistence/history behavior. Keep this out of the #18398 PR.

## Prior art and ownership

An older `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL` matrix has a post-resize variant, but it shrinks its target and is not this warmed-default-target witness. Memory Core `bc1248fd-5441-4f89-82b8-31d4ad72b37e` distinguishes intentional result-region sizing from stale geometry; this failure compares actual host widths, not a retired thin-band expectation. #18121's older native placement/claim instability is separate.

Live latest-20 open, own-assignment and latest-30 all-status A2A sweeps repeated immediately before filing; no equivalent found. Euclid owns the follow-up after the bounded #18398 delivery.
